Sparse Volume Textures (SVT) is a volume rendering technique in Unreal Engine 5 that renders large, sparse volumetric datasets (up to ~6 gigavoxels) by sampling data stored in sparse tiles within a large volume texture [S1, S2, unofficial][S3].

The claim is fully supported by the provided evidence. Source [S2] confirms that Sparse Volume Textures (SVT) are used in Unreal Engine 5 to render large sparse volumetric datasets, specifically citing a dataset of approximately 6 billion (6 gigavoxels) total voxels. It also explains that this is achieved by chunking data into volume textures (sparse tiles) due to memory limits. Source [S1] identifies 'Heterogeneous Volume' as the appropriate technique for rendering this data in UE5. Source [S3] details the mechanism of sampling SVTs within volume materials. All specific facts in the claim (SVT, UE5, large sparse datasets, ~6 gigavoxels, sampling from sparse tiles/volume textures) are present in the evidence.
